name: M33SSS J013359.89+303760.0
description: A Cepheid in the Triangulum Galaxy that pulsates every 6.00 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 5.998 d in Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118, table 9 (log P 0.778); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 5.998 d in Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118, table 9 (log P 0.778); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M33, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2012AJ....144....4M; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118, abstract: M33's Cepheid distance modulus 24.622 +/- 0.03 mag, 10^(mu/5 + 1) pc

text.card: A Cepheid in the Triangulum Galaxy, 840 kiloparsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 6.00 days.
text.introduction: The Hubble Space Telescope measured its brightness in three colours; its pulsation takes 6.00 days. Its galaxy's distance, 840 kiloparsecs, was measured from Cepheids like it.
text.locator: table 9, ID 01335989+3037600: logP; Breuval et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 118: mu

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M33 is not measured
